clue.text: Hair decoration forbidden, say, following a nasty infestation

indicators.note: the sound-alike piece comes after A and LICE, so it follows them

parts.note: lice are a nasty infestation of the hair

indicators.note: say signals that the word for forbidden is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: forbidden means banned

explanation.surface: A hair ornament is banned at school after an outbreak of head lice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you BANNED is only heard, and it sounds like BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alice band is a flexible headband worn to hold the hair back, named after the girl in Tenniel's illustrations.

clue.text: Float freely in the air

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters move about without constraint into a new order

explanation.surface: Something drifts loosely, high above.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft means up high, overhead, so in the air.

clue.text: Couples in car crash in New York covered by one?

definitions.text: Couples in car crash in New York covered by one?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit in the New York abbreviation, inside it
crash suggests the letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: Couples who crash their car in New York hope a policy covers them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges the couples' letters, and 'covered by' puts I above the rest in this down clue; the whole clue then doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Car crash victims would claim on an insurance policy, the contract that covers them against loss.

clue.text: Task for pupil: to cut out holding ruler

indicators.note: one piece holding another contains it

parts.note: to excise is to cut out
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a monarch's cipher, so a ruler

explanation.surface: A school assignment involves cutting things out while gripping a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, from Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen, a ruler; it goes inside EXCISE.
explanation.definitionFit: An exercise is a piece of work set for a pupil to practise a skill, a school task.

clue.text: One regularly in drunken state or states

parts.note: AL is the abbreviation for Alabama, a US state
KY is the abbreviation for Kentucky, another US state

explanation.surface: Someone who is often drunk, in one condition or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but belongs to the definition; 'states' gives two US state codes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alky is slang for an alcoholic, someone who is habitually drunk.

clue.text: Snack cooked by baker unfortunately has burnt topping

parts.note: food that is cooked is done

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something has gone wrong, so the letters come out jumbled
the topping of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A baker has had a mishap and the snack he made is burnt on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' in a down clue means the first letter, here of 'burnt'; the anagram from 'unfortunately' gives RKEBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A doner kebab is slices of spit-roasted meat in pitta bread, a popular takeaway snack.

clue.text: Better to avoid extremes — take a gentle stroll

indicators.note: avoiding the extremes means the word for better loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: Advice that moderation is wise: don't rush, just take a relaxed walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like the comparative of good, but it is a noun: one who bets, GAMBLER, with its first and last letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, leisurely pace, the same as taking a gentle stroll.

clue.text: Witness slattern shedding outer clothing on street

indicators.note: shedding the outer layers strips the word of its two outermost letters at each side

explanation.surface: A slovenly woman strips off her coat in the street before an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding outer clothing' strips two layers of letters from each end of SLATTERN, leaving ATTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to something, to certify that it is true.

clue.text: British request Queen's favourite breed of animal

parts.note: an order is a request for goods
Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was the favourite of Queen Elizabeth I

explanation.surface: A Briton asks for the Queen's preferred breed of livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was Elizabeth I's favourite courtier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Border Leicester is a British breed of sheep, developed in the Scottish Borders.

clue.text: Relaxed about trade being slack in part of holiday?

indicators.note: one piece about another surrounds it

parts.note: easy means relaxed, at ease

indicators.note: slack suggests something loose and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers stay relaxed while business is slow over the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slack' looks like the trade description, but 'being slack' scrambles TRADE into TERDA, which 'about' wraps in EASY.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter Day, Easter Sunday, is one day of the Easter holiday, hence part of it; the question mark admits it is one example.

clue.text: Various pregnant Eskimos acquainted with each other

indicators.note: various suggests the letters are taken in assorted, differing arrangements

explanation.surface: A list of Inuit women expecting babies, who all happen to know one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges all fifteen letters of PREGNANT ESKIMOS.
explanation.definitionFit: People on speaking terms are friendly enough to talk, so they are acquainted with one another.

clue.text: Drivers going through the old country

indicators.note: one piece passing through another means it sits inside it

parts.note: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is the British motorists' organisation, so drivers

explanation.surface: Motorists drive through a land from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British breakdown service; 'going through' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region in the Balkans, home of the Thracians, a country of antiquity.

clue.text: Endless supply of cannabis just making De Quincey at home here

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off the word that follows

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis
just in the sense of mere, only

explanation.surface: An opium-eater's drug supply runs out, and that is all it takes to reach his home.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas De Quincey, the Confessions of an English Opium-Eater author, lived at Dove Cottage in this Lake District village, which neatly fits the drugs surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer Thomas De Quincey lived for years in Dove Cottage in the Lakeland village of Grasmere, after Wordsworth.

clue.text: Points made by public school teachers lacking aspiration at first

indicators.note: aspiration is the sound of H, so lacking it at the start drops the opening letter

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public (private fee-paying) school
heads are head teachers

explanation.surface: Head teachers at an elite school make points without ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English fee-paying school; aspiration is the H sound, which 'lacking aspiration at first' drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowheads are the sharp pointed tips of arrows, so points.

clue.text: TV programme that is taped by clergymen with time to spare

indicators.note: something taped by another is bound inside it
to spare means to be without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: ministers are clergymen
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A clergy team records a television show and still has time left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to spare' drops the T to leave MINISERS; 'taped by' wraps that round the that-is abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniseries is a short television drama shown in a few episodes, a type of TV programme.

clue.text: Canadian fellow seen near Italian port

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A man is spotted beside a harbour in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian port' looks like one idea, but the port is OBAN in Scotland and Italian just gives IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manitoban is a native of Manitoba, a Canadian province, so a Canadian.

clue.text: Achieve turnaround with class dunce

parts.note: cl. is the abbreviation for class

indicators.note: a turnaround means the word for achieve is read backwards

parts.note: to achieve something is to do it

explanation.surface: A poor student manages to turn things round with the help of the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnaround' reverses the achieve word, giving OD.
explanation.definitionFit: A clod is a dull, stupid person, the same as a dunce or blockhead.

clue.text: Bound to be in trouble for this?

definitions.text: Bound to be in trouble for this?

parts.words: Bound to be in trouble for this?
parts.note: someone due a punishment is said to be in line for an athletics event; that event is also a bound, an upward leap over a bar

explanation.definitionFit: Being for the high jump is a British idiom for facing punishment, and the athletic event is a single upward bound.

clue.text: Coward for one left taking a long time to retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so both pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period of time

explanation.surface: A coward leaves, taking ages to back away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like an insult, but it means the playwright Noel Coward, so the answer is his first name. L then EON gives LEON, and 'to retreat' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright Sir Noel Coward is an example of someone bearing this first name.

clue.text: VIP's lack of expertise?

parts.note: lack of something is not having it, so a plain no or not
expertise is skill or ability

explanation.surface: A jibe that a celebrity has no real talent.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay; the question mark flags the whimsical split.
explanation.definitionFit: A notability is a notable or famous person, a celebrity or very important person.

clue.text: Wants the original Calendar Girls?

parts.note: the original Calendar Girls were members of the Women's Institute, abbreviated WI
shes, as a noun, are females, girls

explanation.surface: A question about what the famous fundraising calendar women desired.
explanation.walkthrough: The Calendar Girls were Women's Institute members in Yorkshire who posed nude for a charity calendar; the Women's Institute is a British women's organisation, WI.
explanation.definitionFit: Wishes and wants are both desires or things longed for.

clue.text: Ultra-Conservative? Indeed

definitions.meaning: excessively right-wing in politics, more to the right than is reasonable
an emphatic Australian and British exclamation of agreement, like absolutely

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means excessively right-wing; as an idiom it is an emphatic yes, you bet.

clue.text: Self-possession shown by elected leader, concealing set-back at hospital

indicators.note: one piece concealing another holds it inside

parts.note: PM, Prime Minister, is the elected leader of a British government
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: back means the word for set is read in reverse

parts.note: to set, as a jelly does, is to gel

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister keeps calm while hiding a setback during a hospital visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GEL into LEG; 'concealing' puts the hospital letter and that inside the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm in its older sense is calmness of temper, coolness, which is self-possession.

clue.text: Girl is a bit of a human dynamo

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase is a run of its letters taken from inside

explanation.surface: A girl is described as a real live wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandy is a girl's name, a short form of Amanda.

clue.text: After holiday's over you'll need a sparkling drink

indicators.note: over means turned over, read backwards

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a holiday

explanation.surface: Once the holiday is finished you will want a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: VAC turned over gives CAV, followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is a Spanish sparkling wine, so a sparkling drink.

clue.text: Alert, when a cigarette end is dropped in Sussex town

indicators.note: pieces dropped in another word are placed inside it

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside town in Sussex, on England's south coast
as can mean when, as in as I left
a butt is the stub end of a smoked cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone watchful when a cigarette stub is tossed away in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside resort in Sussex; 'dropped in' places the cigarette stub, with 'when' and 'a', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright as a button is an idiom for lively and quick-witted, so alert.

clue.text: Poet giving contradictory answers to question

parts.note: no is one answer to a question
yes is the opposite answer to a question

explanation.surface: A poet dithers, answering a question both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet best known for the ballad The Highwayman, an example of a poet.

clue.text: Role in dramatic event before wedding

indicators.note: one piece in another is placed inside it

parts.note: stagy means theatrical, dramatic
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: Someone has a part in a theatrical show held ahead of a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is the groom's celebration with male friends shortly before his marriage.
